header: This is the SECOND line of defence for LLM-written SQL; the FIRST is the database itself: a read-only transaction, a role that can only SELECT from three views, and a statement timeout (see executor.ts and sql/01_*.sql). Here I parse the SQL with a real PostgreSQL parser and walk the whole syntax tree. The guard accepts ONE read-only statement that touches only the approved views and calls only approved functions. Anything it cannot parse or cannot positively approve is rejected: the model is then told why and gets to try again (see generator.ts). I keep it strict on purpose, because a too-strict rejection costs one retry, while a too-lenient one could cost real damage. Strict wins.

symbols.name: GuardResult
symbols.sig: { ok: true; sql: string } | { ok: false; reason: string }

symbols.name: ALLOWED_RELATIONS
doc: I let the model read only these relations.

symbols.name: NLQ_FUNCTIONS
doc: These are my own helper functions, callable as nlq.<name>.

symbols.name: ALLOWED_FUNCTIONS
doc: Built-in functions the model may call. I keep this a deliberately short allow-list: no pg_sleep, set_config, pg_read_file, nextval, dblink, lo_*, etc.

symbols.name: stripLiterals
doc: I remove '...' string literals and "..." quoted identifiers first, so the structural checks (comments, semicolons) do not trip over their contents.
